title: K-flat tensor comparison for augmented derived Roos fibres
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,R)$ be a ringed site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use the unbounded derived category $D(R)$ with localization $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], signed direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and derived products [def-weil-category-product]. Let $A$ be a K-flat complex of $R$-module sheaves [def-pc-kflat-complex], and write $T_A=QA\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}-$, computed by $\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_R-)$.

Let $X=(X_n,t_n)$ be a strict tower of complexes [def-weil-inverse-system] and choose a K-injective [def-pur-kinjective-complex] tower resolution $X\to I$ with injective terms. Total right derived inverse limit $L(X)$ is $Q\lim_n I_n$; its natural Roos realization is the fibre of $1-s$ on the derived product [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Put $(A\otimes X)_n=\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_R X_n)$ with transitions $1_A\otimes t_n$. There is a natural morphism
$$\beta_{A,X}:T_A L(X)\longrightarrow L(A\otimes X)$$
with the following resolution normalization. Choose a K-injective tower resolution $A\otimes I\to J$ with injective terms, with components $q_n$. Put $P_I=\prod_n I_n$, $P_J=\prod_nJ_n$ (termwise products), and let
$$b:\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_RP_I)\longrightarrow P_J$$
be the chain map with $n$-th projection $q_n(1_A\otimes\mathrm{pr}_n)$. For a tower $V$, write $H(V)^k=P_V^k\oplus P_V^{k-1}$ with differential $d(x,y)=(dx,(1-s)x-dy)$. Via $L(X)\cong QH(I)$ and $L(A\otimes X)\cong QH(J)$, the morphism $\beta_{A,X}$ is represented by the chain map
$$\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_R H(I))\longrightarrow H(J),\qquad
 a\otimes(x,y)\longmapsto\bigl(b(a\otimes x),(-1)^p b(a\otimes y)\bigr)\quad(a\in A^p).$$
Here the formula specifies the two summand maps of the total complex. These localized morphisms are independent of the chosen resolutions, natural in strict tower maps and K-flat tensor arguments, and compatible with quasi-isomorphisms in either argument.

If the canonical derived product map
$$T_A\bigl(\prod_n^D QX_n\bigr)\longrightarrow\prod_n^D T_A(QX_n),\qquad \mathrm{pr}_n\circ\phi=T_A(\mathrm{pr}_n),$$
is an isomorphism, then $\beta_{A,X}$ is an isomorphism. No exactness of countable products of module sheaves is assumed.

For a complex $Z$ and a strict augmentation $\gamma:\Delta Z\to X$, let $a_\gamma:QZ\to L(X)$ be the canonical augmented derived-limit map: on a resolution it is the compatible-family map into the ordinary limit followed by its derived comparison, equivalently the Roos map with coordinates $((\gamma_n)_n,0)$ after composing into $I$. Let $a_{A\otimes\gamma}:Q\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_R Z)\to L(A\otimes X)$ be defined identically. Then, under the K-flat computation identification,
$$\beta_{A,X}\circ T_A(a_\gamma)=a_{A\otimes\gamma}.$$
This is equality of the whole maps into the normalized derived inverse limit, including the zero shifted-product coordinate, not just equality of their projections.

split_report.summary: Kept the full statement. Constructed the comparison into resolved ordinary limits, proved its choice independence and naturality using K-injective Hom bijections and explicit compatible homotopies, identified the exact signed Roos formula by the normalized kernel inclusions, and checked the product-isomorphism criterion and the whole strict-augmentation identity. Reused existing general tools; no new nodes are needed.

tool_uses.why: Signed total tensor, homotopies, cones and K-flat quasi-isomorphism preservation on arbitrary ringed sites; a generic homological tool, not a replacement for the integral tensor route.
Total derived inverse limit of strict ringed-site towers, computed on K-injective tower resolutions; needed to normalize the actual comparison.
Injective tower transitions split and the specified kernel inclusion computes the Roos fibre and derived products without AB4*; generic resolution normalization.
Hom into K-injectives computes derived Hom, hence existence and uniqueness up to homotopy of tower resolution comparisons.
Resolve an arbitrary module-sheaf complex K-flatly to verify quasi-isomorphism invariance in the K-flat tensor argument.
Tower category is abelian with exact evaluation, so quasi-isomorphisms and homotopies used in the comparison are tower-theoretic.
Two isomorphic product components in the specified morphism of distinguished triangles imply the fibre component is invertible.

Checked: (1) the H(V) differential squares to zero, and the coordinate change (y,x)->(x,-y) from the roos-shifts convention d(y,x)=(-dy-hx,dx) gives exactly (dx,(1-s)x-dy). (2) F_J b=b(1⊗F_I), checked projection by projection from t^J q_{n+1}=q_n(1⊗t^I_n). (3) Psi with the (-1)^p sign is a chain map; both second coordinates equal b(a⊗Fx)-b(a⊗dy)-(-1)^p b(da⊗y). (4) The K-injective Hom bijection in Tow(Mod R) gives u and v, unique up to homotopy; the compatible homotopy tuple h_n(1⊗π_n) gives resolution independence and naturality. (5) The iso criterion is robust: Psi = fib(b)∘φ' with φ' a chain iso, (fib(b),b,b) is a strict morphism of rotated cone triangles, Qb is the canonical product map by uniqueness of product maps, and lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso applies. (6) The augmentation identity θ(A⊗c)=(q_n(1⊗c_n)) holds strictly before localization, with second coordinate 0. Edge cases: A=0, X=0, A=R[1] (minus sign), constant tower, zero γ. The step-1 three-sided square with a K-flat resolution is valid.
